newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end firm, aided by US rate decision - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end firm, aided by US rate decision - Sept 24.

text.p: Chilean blue chip shares closed broadly higher in calm trade with investors reassured by the Federal Reserve's decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged, said dealers.
The bolsa is expected to open slightly higher with turnover boosted by month-end portfolio adjustments by institutional investors, they said.
The selective IPSA index closed unofficially up 0.36 percent at 99.49 points. The general IGPA index gained 0.35 percent to 5,473.22 points.
The market continued to be buoyed by July's surprisingly soft economic data which has given rise to hopes the Central Bank could cut interest rates towards the year-end, they said.
The government Imacec index showed July growth at 5.8 percent, sharply below forecasts for around seven percent.
But the optimism could be premature. The July figure was skewed by a sharp fall as the result of a slide in copper exports.
"If you remove copper from the calculation, the growth rate is still high," said one dealer.
Central Bank officials have said the August Imacec figure will also be low as the result of a drop in copper exports.
Gainers included forestry stocks Copec and CMPC which rose on speculation that one of the firms may be successful in its bid for the state-owned Alto Parana pulp plant in Argentina, said traders.
Both companies have made offers for the plant which is said to be worth around $200 million.
Copec firmed 2.01 percent at 1,775 pesos, while CMPC rose 1.25 percent to 5,245 pesos.
Losers included winery Concha y Toro, down 1.86 percent at 158 pesos, drug-maker LabChile, down 1.49 percent at 330 pesos and power utility Enersis, which fell 0.39 percent to 256 pesos.
